purpose: machine-readable ontology of methods for faithfully extracting, reconstructing, diagramming, and formalizing the structure of real arguments (Toulmin model, structure types, enthymeme reconstruction, argumentation schemes, and pragma-dialectical critical discussion), as a subdomain node of argumentation & critical reasoning for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: Argument mapping is modeled as a subdomain of argumentation and critical reasoning.
Nodes are concrete, evaluable representation/reconstruction methods, not topics to read about.
No observed dataset or experimental evidence is supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors.
Scope follows Toulmin (2003), van Eemeren & Grootendorst (2004), Walton, Reed & Macagno (2008), and Freeman (2011).
exclusions: Formal/symbolic proof theory and deductive validity calculi as ends in themselves.
Rhetorical persuasion technique and style independent of structure.
Natural-language-processing model training for automated argument mining.

competency_questions.question: Which spans of a passage are argumentative and which statements are premises versus the conclusion?
How is the main conclusion identified and each statement assigned an inferential role?
Does the argument contain intermediate conclusions forming a serial chain, and how is the chain ordered?
Which unstated premises must be supplied to complete an enthymeme, and how is charity bounded?
How is the reconstruction kept faithful to the arguer while being made reasonably strong?
Are co-premises linked or convergent, and how is that decided?
How are objections, rebuttals, and undercutters represented in the map?
How is the reconstructed structure rendered as a diagram and validated against the typed structure?
In what notation or tool is the map serialized for sharing and interchange?
How is an argument mapped onto the Toulmin claim/data/warrant core?
How are the warrant's backing, the claim's qualifier, and its rebuttal modeled?
Which argumentation scheme fits the inference and how are its slots bound?
How is the reconstructed argument evaluated, including the burden of proof per premise?
How is a dispute reconstructed as a critical discussion with stages and rules?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PD stage and rule nodes present

glossary.definition: a diagram of statements connected by typed support and attack relations
a statement offered as a reason supporting a conclusion
a statement an argument seeks to establish from its premises
an argument with one or more premises (or the conclusion) left unstated
premises that must work jointly to support a conclusion
premises that each independently support the same conclusion
the inferential license permitting the move from data to claim
the field-dependent support that establishes a warrant's authority
conditions of exception under which the warrant does not license the claim
a stereotyped pattern of defeasible reasoning with associated critical questions
the standard questions that probe and can defeat a scheme-based inference
the pragma-dialectical ideal model of resolving a difference of opinion through four stages
an attack on the inferential link rather than on the conclusion

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established argument-mapping and argumentation-theory literature (Toulmin 2003; van Eemeren & Grootendorst 2004; Walton, Reed & Macagno 2008; Freeman 2011) and analytic practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Locate and delimit the argumentative spans in a passage, separating argument-bearing text from narration, explanation, description, and report.
contradictors: reader who treats every sentence as a premise

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the passage is re-segmented or new source text is added

pros.claim: everything downstream operates only on genuinely argumentative material
pros.example: an indicator like 'therefore' flags an inference to extract

cons.claim: over-extraction pulls in explanations that are not arguments
cons.example: treating a causal explanation of an accepted fact as an argument

acceptance_tests: each extracted span contains at least one inferential move
non-argument material is explicitly excluded with reason
revisit_triggers: discourse purpose reinterpreted as explanation vs argument

nodes.definition: Classify each extracted statement as a conclusion (claim) or a premise (reason), assigning inferential role rather than surface position.
contradictors: reader who assumes the last sentence is always the conclusion

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an indicator word is found to mark a conclusion previously read as a premise

pros.claim: role assignment is the backbone every later structure inherits
pros.example: 'since' marks a premise; 'so' marks the conclusion it supports

cons.claim: mis-assigning the main conclusion inverts the whole map
cons.example: reading a restated premise as the thesis

acceptance_tests: each statement has exactly one inferential role or is flagged as dual-role
the main conclusion is identified and justified

nodes.definition: Distinguish the final (main) conclusion from intermediate conclusions that serve as premises for further inference, building the inferential chain.
contradictors: reader who flattens a chain into one inference step

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a statement is found to be both supported and supporting (an intermediate conclusion)

pros.claim: exposes multi-step reasoning that a flat map would hide
pros.example: a sub-conclusion supports the main thesis and is itself supported

cons.claim: missing an intermediate conclusion collapses a serial structure
cons.example: treating a lemma as a free-standing premise

failure_modes: intermediate conclusion treated as a primitive premise
acceptance_tests: every intermediate conclusion is both a target and a source of inference
the single final conclusion is unique
revisit_triggers: a new inferential step is discovered

nodes.definition: Rewrite each premise and conclusion as a clear, self-contained declarative proposition, resolving pronouns, rhetorical questions, and ellipsis without changing meaning.
contradictors: analyst who diagrams raw verbatim text

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a paraphrase is challenged as altering the original claim

pros.claim: clear propositions make inferential links checkable
pros.example: rewriting 'Isn't that obviously unfair?' as 'That policy is unfair'

cons.claim: aggressive paraphrase can smuggle in or strip content
cons.example: strengthening a vague claim into a stronger one the author never made

failure_modes: loss of hedges or modal qualification
acceptance_tests: each proposition is declarative and self-contained
paraphrase preserves the author's commitment

nodes.definition: Supply the unstated premises (or unstated conclusion) needed to make an enthymematic argument complete, guided by the principle of charity.
contradictors: literalist who refuses to add any unstated premise
outputs: explicit list of added implicit premises

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a supplied premise is contested as uncharitable or as a straw addition

pros.claim: makes a gappy argument evaluable without distorting it
pros.example: adding the suppressed major premise of a categorical syllogism

cons.claim: over-supplying premises can build a stronger or weaker argument than intended
cons.example: inserting a false universal to make the argument look fallacious

failure_modes: steel reconstruction beyond the author's commitment
acceptance_tests: each added premise is necessary for the inference and minimally strong
supplied premises are plausibly attributable to the arguer

nodes.definition: Govern reconstruction so the mapped argument stays faithful to the arguer's actual commitments while being made as strong as the text reasonably allows.
contradictors: debater who deliberately reconstructs the weakest reading

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the reconstruction diverges from the arguer's evident intent

pros.claim: prevents both straw-man and straw-steel distortions of the source
pros.example: rejecting an added premise the author would clearly disown

cons.claim: excessive charity can rewrite a bad argument into a good one the author never gave
cons.example: supplying a sophisticated premise a layperson never intended

acceptance_tests: every reconstruction step traces to a textual or contextual warrant
distortions are flagged not silently fixed

nodes.definition: Classify how premises support a conclusion as convergent, linked, serial, or divergent/branching, fixing the topology of support.
contradictors: analyst who joins all premises with one arrow regardless of structure

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a premise set is reanalyzed from convergent to linked or vice versa

pros.claim: the topology determines how the map is drawn and evaluated
pros.example: two independent reasons are convergent; co-dependent reasons are linked

cons.claim: mis-typing linked vs convergent misstates how attacking one premise affects support
cons.example: drawing co-dependent premises as independent overstates robustness

failure_modes: divergent support for multiple conclusions collapsed
acceptance_tests: each inference is typed as convergent, linked, serial, or divergent
the typing matches the dependency among premises

nodes.definition: Apply an operational test (e.g., the Suppression/Independence test) to decide whether co-premises are linked (jointly required) or convergent (independently sufficient).
contradictors: analyst who defaults all multi-premise support to convergent

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when removing one premise is found to destroy rather than weaken support

pros.claim: resolves the hardest recurring structural ambiguity with a repeatable test
pros.example: if dropping a premise leaves no support, the premises are linked

cons.claim: the test gives indeterminate results for some premise sets
cons.example: borderline cases where partial support remains after removal

acceptance_tests: each multi-premise inference has a stated linked/convergent verdict
the verdict cites the applied test

nodes.definition: Represent attacks on the argument: rebutting defeaters (counter-conclusions), undercutting defeaters (attacks on the inference), and counter-considerations.
contradictors: analyst who maps only the pro side

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a previously ignored objection or undercutter is found in the source

pros.claim: captures defeasibility instead of a one-sided pro map
pros.example: an exception clause undercuts a defeasible inference

cons.claim: conflating a rebuttal (attacks conclusion) with an undercutter (attacks the link) misstates the dialectic
cons.example: drawing an inference-attack as a counter-premise to the conclusion

acceptance_tests: each attack is typed as rebut or undercut and aimed at the correct target
counter-considerations are linked to what they oppose

nodes.definition: Render the reconstructed argument as a node-and-arrow diagram in which boxes are statements and arrows encode typed support and attack relations.
contradictors: analyst who keeps structure only in prose

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the diagram conflicts with the underlying typed structure

pros.claim: a faithful diagram makes the inferential skeleton inspectable at a glance
pros.example: linked premises joined under one inference node, convergent ones with separate arrows

cons.claim: a tidy-looking diagram can hide a wrong structural typing
cons.example: a clean chart that mislabels linked support as convergent

acceptance_tests: every box and arrow corresponds to a typed statement or relation
the diagram reproduces the linked/convergent/serial topology

nodes.definition: Choose the notation and tool for serializing the map (e.g., Argument Markup Language, Araucaria/OVA, Rationale-style boxes) and produce a portable representation.
contradictors: analyst who hand-draws maps with no shared schema
outputs: serialized map in a chosen notation

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when interchange with another tool or corpus standard is required

pros.claim: a standard notation makes maps shareable, comparable, and machine-processable
pros.example: exporting to AIF lets the map be reused across tools

cons.claim: premature tool lock can force the analysis into an ill-fitting schema
cons.example: a tool that cannot express undercutters distorts the map

failure_modes: notation cannot express a needed relation type
tool-specific artifacts leak into the analysis
acceptance_tests: the chosen notation can express every relation in the map
the serialization round-trips without loss
revisit_triggers: map gains relation types the tool lacks

nodes.definition: Map an argument onto the Toulmin core of claim, data/grounds, and warrant, separating what is asserted from the evidence and the inferential license.
contradictors: formal logician who rejects field-dependent warrants

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when grounds and warrant are found to be conflated in the mapping

pros.claim: separates the evidence (data) from the inference license (warrant)
pros.example: 'Harry was born in Bermuda' is data; 'people born in Bermuda are British' is the warrant

cons.claim: forcing every argument into Toulmin slots can be procrustean
cons.example: squeezing a multi-premise chain into a single warrant

acceptance_tests: claim, data, and warrant are each populated and distinct
the warrant licenses the move from data to claim

nodes.definition: Make the (often implicit) warrant explicit and identify its backing: the field-dependent body of support that establishes the warrant's authority.
contradictors: analyst who states warrants without backing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the backing for a warrant is challenged or found to be field-inappropriate

pros.claim: exposes the inferential license and the discipline-specific support behind it
pros.example: a statute backs the warrant in a legal argument

cons.claim: warrants and their backing are easy to confuse with ordinary premises
cons.example: listing the backing as just another datum

acceptance_tests: the warrant is stated explicitly and is distinct from the data
the backing is field-appropriate to the warrant

nodes.definition: Represent the qualifier (the strength/modality of the claim) and the rebuttal (conditions of exception that defeat the warrant) in the Toulmin layout.
contradictors: analyst who treats all claims as unqualified

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a hedge or exception in the source is found unmodeled

pros.claim: captures that real arguments are defeasible and qualified, not deductive certainties
pros.example: 'presumably' qualifies the claim; 'unless naturalized' is the rebuttal

cons.claim: qualifiers and rebuttals are routinely dropped, overstating conclusions
cons.example: reading a hedged claim as a categorical one

acceptance_tests: the claim's qualifier matches the source modality
known exception conditions appear as rebuttals

nodes.definition: Match the reconstructed inference to an argumentation scheme (e.g., expert opinion, analogy, cause-to-effect, practical reasoning) as a stereotyped reasoning template.
contradictors: deductivist who recognizes only formal valid forms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the inference fits a different scheme than first assigned

pros.claim: a scheme supplies the template and the critical questions to test the inference
pros.example: 'experts say X, so X' is the argument-from-expert-opinion scheme

cons.claim: forcing an inference into the wrong scheme imports the wrong critical questions
cons.example: labeling a sign argument as cause-to-effect

failure_modes: scheme slots bound to the wrong statements
acceptance_tests: the assigned scheme's premise slots are all bound to statements
the inference matches the scheme's pattern

nodes.definition: Apply the critical questions attached to the selected scheme to probe the inference and surface the burden of proof for each presumptive premise.
contradictors: analyst who accepts a scheme match as a verdict

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when an unanswered critical question reopens the inference

pros.claim: turns a scheme match into an evaluation by asking what could defeat it
pros.example: for expert opinion: is the source a genuine, unbiased expert in the field?

cons.claim: applying the wrong scheme's questions misdirects scrutiny
cons.example: asking cause-questions of an argument from analogy

acceptance_tests: each critical question for the scheme is answered or flagged unmet
unmet questions are recorded as defeaters

nodes.definition: Identify the standpoints and the difference of opinion at issue (the confrontation stage), fixing what is being disputed and by whom.
contradictors: analyst who maps an argument with no opposing standpoint

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the standpoint or the disputed proposition is reframed

pros.claim: locates the actual point of dispute that the argumentation must resolve
pros.example: a mixed dispute has both parties defending opposing standpoints

cons.claim: mis-stating the standpoint mis-scopes the entire critical discussion
cons.example: analyzing support for a standpoint no one actually holds

failure_modes: difference of opinion mis-typed (single vs mixed)
acceptance_tests: each standpoint and its holder is stated
the difference of opinion is typed

nodes.definition: Map the discourse onto the four stages of a critical discussion - confrontation, opening, argumentation, and concluding - to reconstruct its dialectical structure.
contradictors: monological analyst who ignores dialogue stages

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a discourse move is reassigned to a different discussion stage

pros.claim: reconstructs argumentation as a regulated dispute-resolution procedure
pros.example: the opening stage fixes the shared premises and procedural rules

cons.claim: real discourse rarely maps cleanly onto idealized stages
cons.example: forcing scattered remarks into a tidy four-stage sequence

acceptance_tests: each relevant move is assigned to a discussion stage
the analytic overview covers all four stages

nodes.definition: Check moves against the rules for critical discussion and reconstruct fallacies as rule violations that obstruct resolving the difference of opinion.
contradictors: analyst who treats fallacies only as invalid forms

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a move previously accepted is found to violate a discussion rule

pros.claim: diagnoses fallacies functionally as derailments of the discussion
pros.example: an ad hominem violates the freedom rule by silencing a party

cons.claim: rule violations require the reconstructed stage context to be correct first
cons.example: calling a move fallacious without establishing the stage it occurs in

failure_modes: violation attributed to the wrong rule or stage
acceptance_tests: each alleged fallacy is tied to a specific violated rule
the violated rule is appropriate to the discussion stage

nodes.definition: Validate the finished map for internal coherence: role consistency, structural-typing fidelity, no dangling or circular support, and faithful slot bindings.
contradictors: analyst who ships the first-draft map unchecked

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a coherence check fails after any upstream reconstruction change

pros.claim: catches structural errors before the map is used for evaluation or handoff
pros.example: detecting a premise that supports nothing and a circular support loop

cons.claim: coherence checking validates form, not the truth of premises
cons.example: a perfectly coherent map of a false-premised argument

failure_modes: dangling node left in the map
acceptance_tests: no statement is unsupported-and-unused or part of a support cycle
the diagram matches the typed structure and slot bindings

nodes.definition: Evaluate the reconstructed argument against acceptability, relevance, and sufficiency (RSA) criteria, producing the assessment the map was built to support.
contradictors: mapper who stops at structure and never evaluates

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when premise acceptability or sufficiency is reassessed against new evidence

pros.claim: delivers the actual judgment of how good the argument is, grounded in the map
pros.example: premises acceptable and relevant but jointly insufficient for the claim

cons.claim: an evaluation is only as sound as the reconstruction it rests on
cons.example: a confident verdict built on an uncharitable reconstruction

failure_modes: conflating acceptability with relevance or sufficiency
acceptance_tests: each premise is judged on acceptability and relevance
the premises' joint sufficiency for the conclusion is assessed

edges.why_related: role assignment operates on the extracted argumentative spans
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clean extraction prevents typing non-argument text
edges.risk_of_conflict: typing before extraction processes irrelevant material
edges.example: extract the argument before classifying statement roles

edges.why_related: the conclusion hierarchy is built from assigned roles
edges.benefit_of_coupling: roles fix which statements can be intermediate conclusions
edges.risk_of_conflict: hierarchy without roles is unfounded
edges.example: assign roles before building the chain

edges.why_related: standardization rewrites the role-assigned statements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: standardizing typed statements keeps roles intact
edges.risk_of_conflict: rewriting before typing can blur roles
edges.example: type statements before standardizing them

edges.why_related: premises are supplied against standardized propositions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clear propositions reveal what is missing
edges.risk_of_conflict: supplying premises to vague text adds noise
edges.example: standardize before adding implicit premises

edges.why_related: the hierarchy shows which inferential gaps need premises
edges.benefit_of_coupling: known chain locates each gap
edges.risk_of_conflict: adding premises without the chain misplaces them
edges.example: fix the chain before filling gaps

edges.why_related: the charity control audits the supplied premises
edges.benefit_of_coupling: auditing additions prevents distortion
edges.risk_of_conflict: unaudited additions can straw-man or steel-man
edges.example: audit every supplied premise for charity and fidelity
edges.resolution_rule: audit additions before they enter the map

edges.why_related: structure typing needs the conclusion hierarchy in place
edges.benefit_of_coupling: known intermediate conclusions enable serial typing
edges.risk_of_conflict: typing without the hierarchy mislabels serial steps
edges.example: fix the hierarchy before typing support

edges.why_related: typing depends on clearly stated premises
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clear premises make dependency visible
edges.risk_of_conflict: typing vague premises misreads dependency
edges.example: standardize before typing

edges.why_related: the test refines the convergent/linked typing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the test resolves typing ambiguity
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying the test out of context misleads
edges.example: type first, then apply the test to ambiguous sets

edges.why_related: attacks are attached to typed inferences and conclusions
edges.benefit_of_coupling: typed structure shows what an attack targets
edges.risk_of_conflict: attaching attacks before typing misaims them
edges.example: type the support before modeling attacks

edges.why_related: the diagram renders the typed structure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: typed topology determines the layout
edges.risk_of_conflict: diagramming before typing produces a wrong picture
edges.example: finalize typing before drawing

edges.why_related: diagram boxes are the role-assigned statements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: roles label the boxes correctly
edges.risk_of_conflict: unlabeled boxes misrepresent roles
edges.example: assign roles before drawing boxes

edges.why_related: attack arrows are added to the diagram
edges.benefit_of_coupling: including attacks completes the map
edges.risk_of_conflict: omitting attacks yields a one-sided map
edges.example: model attacks before finalizing the diagram

edges.why_related: serialization encodes the drawn diagram
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a diagram fixes what the notation must express
edges.risk_of_conflict: choosing notation before the diagram risks misfit
edges.example: draw before serializing

edges.why_related: Toulmin slots are filled from role-assigned, standardized statements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: roles seed the claim and data slots
edges.risk_of_conflict: filling slots before typing confuses data and claim
edges.example: assign roles before Toulmin mapping

edges.why_related: clean propositions populate the Toulmin slots
edges.benefit_of_coupling: clear statements separate data from warrant
edges.risk_of_conflict: vague statements blur the slots
edges.example: standardize before slotting

edges.why_related: backing reconstruction extends the warrant slot
edges.benefit_of_coupling: an explicit warrant enables finding its backing
edges.risk_of_conflict: seeking backing without a stated warrant is unfocused
edges.example: state the warrant before its backing

edges.why_related: qualifier and rebuttal attach to the warranted claim
edges.benefit_of_coupling: an explicit warrant shows its exception conditions
edges.risk_of_conflict: qualifiers without the warrant context float free
edges.example: fix the warrant before its qualifier and rebuttal

edges.why_related: scheme matching applies to a typed inference
edges.benefit_of_coupling: typed inferences narrow the candidate schemes
edges.risk_of_conflict: scheme-matching untyped inferences misfires
edges.example: type the inference before scheme selection

edges.why_related: scheme slots bind to role-assigned statements
edges.benefit_of_coupling: roles indicate which premise fills which slot
edges.risk_of_conflict: binding slots to mis-typed statements is wrong
edges.example: assign roles before binding scheme slots

edges.why_related: the critical questions come from the selected scheme
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a correct scheme supplies the right questions
edges.risk_of_conflict: applying questions without a scheme is undirected
edges.example: select the scheme before its critical questions

edges.why_related: standpoints are identified from the extracted discourse
edges.benefit_of_coupling: extraction supplies the disputed material
edges.risk_of_conflict: identifying standpoints before extraction is premature
edges.example: extract discourse before naming standpoints

edges.why_related: stage mapping needs the standpoints and difference of opinion
edges.benefit_of_coupling: the confrontation fixes what the stages resolve
edges.risk_of_conflict: stage mapping without standpoints is unanchored
edges.example: fix standpoints before mapping stages

edges.why_related: rule checking presupposes the stage assignment
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stage context determines which rule applies
edges.risk_of_conflict: judging violations without stages mislabels fallacies
edges.example: assign stages before checking rules

edges.why_related: validation operates on the produced map
edges.benefit_of_coupling: a built map can be checked for coherence
edges.risk_of_conflict: validating before a map exists is empty
edges.example: build the map before validating it

edges.why_related: coherence checks the typed structure for consistency
edges.benefit_of_coupling: typed structure is the validation target
edges.risk_of_conflict: checking coherence without typing is shallow
edges.example: finalize typing before coherence validation

edges.why_related: evaluation runs only on a coherent, validated map
edges.benefit_of_coupling: coherence prevents evaluating a malformed map
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating an incoherent map yields a meaningless verdict
edges.example: validate coherence before evaluating

edges.why_related: the evaluation incorporates unmet critical questions as defeaters
edges.benefit_of_coupling: answered critical questions feed the verdict
edges.risk_of_conflict: evaluating without the critical questions ignores defeaters
edges.example: apply critical questions before the final verdict

edges.why_related: the verdict weighs modeled rebuttals and undercutters
edges.benefit_of_coupling: modeled attacks inform sufficiency judgment
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring attacks overstates the argument
edges.example: model attacks before evaluating

edges.why_related: charity bounds how much may be supplied
edges.benefit_of_coupling: keeps reconstruction faithful and minimal
edges.risk_of_conflict: unbounded supply distorts the argument
edges.example: limit additions to what charity and fidelity allow

edges.why_related: the claim's qualifier bounds how strong a verdict may be
edges.benefit_of_coupling: prevents overstating an evaluation
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the qualifier inflates the conclusion
edges.example: bound the verdict by the claim's qualifier

edges.why_related: fidelity constrains which scheme may be attributed
edges.benefit_of_coupling: prevents attributing an unintended scheme
edges.risk_of_conflict: attributing a scheme the arguer did not use distorts intent
edges.example: attribute only schemes consistent with the source

edges.why_related: maximal charity in reconstruction tensions with critical evaluation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: names the charity-vs-critique tradeoff
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-charity rewrites a weak argument; under-charity straw-mans it
edges.example: reconstruct charitably but evaluate the arguer's actual commitment, not an improved one
edges.resolution_rule: when charity and critique conflict, fix the most defensible attributable reading then evaluate it

edges.why_related: adding an implicit premise can flip a convergent set into a linked one
edges.benefit_of_coupling: names the completeness-vs-structure tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: premises added for completeness silently change the support topology
edges.example: re-type the structure after any premise is supplied
edges.resolution_rule: after supplying premises, re-run structure typing before locking the map

edges.why_related: Toulmin warrant analysis and scheme templates can carve the same inference differently
edges.benefit_of_coupling: names the framework-choice tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: mixing a Toulmin warrant and a scheme inconsistently double-counts the inference
edges.example: pick the primary framework per inference and map the other as an annotation
edges.resolution_rule: choose one primary framework per inference; cross-reference the other rather than duplicating it

edges.why_related: tool/notation limits can force simplification of the drawn structure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: names the fidelity-vs-portability tension
edges.risk_of_conflict: a notation that cannot express undercutters drops them from the serialized map
edges.example: prefer a notation expressive enough for the map; otherwise annotate the lost relations
edges.resolution_rule: if the notation cannot express a relation, keep the richer diagram authoritative and record the gap

edges.why_related: both decompose an inference, one by functional slot and one by support topology
edges.benefit_of_coupling: cross-checking the two decompositions catches errors
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as interchangeable conflates slot and topology
edges.example: use each for its purpose; reconcile, do not merge
edges.resolution_rule: keep slot-based and topology-based views distinct but mutually consistent

edges.why_related: a failed evaluation can reopen the reconstruction
edges.benefit_of_coupling: lets a discovered gap trigger re-reconstruction
edges.risk_of_conflict: looping forever on re-reconstruction stalls the analysis
edges.example: revisit reconstruction only on a material evaluation defect
edges.resolution_rule: stop when no material defect remains or after two reconstruction passes

edges.why_related: an unanswerable critical question can signal the wrong scheme
edges.benefit_of_coupling: lets question failure trigger re-selection
edges.risk_of_conflict: endless re-selection prevents closure
edges.example: re-select the scheme only when its critical questions systematically fail
edges.resolution_rule: stop after the scheme whose critical questions are best satisfied is found, or after two re-selections

edges.why_related: a coherence failure can send typing back for repair
edges.benefit_of_coupling: lets structural defects trigger re-typing
edges.risk_of_conflict: repeated re-typing without convergence loops
edges.example: re-type only on a detected structural inconsistency
edges.resolution_rule: stop when the diagram matches the typed structure or after two re-typing passes

conflict_axes.trigger: making the argument as strong as possible conflicts with criticizing the argument actually given
resolution_order: fix the strongest reading attributable to the arguer
evaluate that reading, not an improved one
record any charitable additions
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: charity governs reconstruction; the evaluated object is the arguer's actual commitment, not a better argument the analyst invented
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if charity would supply a premise the arguer would disown
conflict_axes.example: strengthening a fallacious argument into a valid one

conflict_axes.trigger: completing the structure requires additions the text does not state
resolution_order: add only premises necessary for the inference
mark each addition as supplied
prefer the minimally strong addition
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: fidelity dominates: additions are minimal, flagged, and attributable, never silent
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a needed addition has no textual or contextual warrant
conflict_axes.example: inserting a controversial universal to complete a syllogism

conflict_axes.trigger: co-premises admit both a jointly-required and an independently-sufficient reading
resolution_order: apply the independence/suppression test
adopt the verdict the test yields
document indeterminate cases as a caveat
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the test verdict dominates a default; unresolved cases are reported as structurally ambiguous
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the test is indeterminate for a decision-critical inference
conflict_axes.example: two reasons that may or may not each suffice alone

conflict_axes.trigger: the same inference can be cast as a Toulmin warrant or as an argumentation scheme
resolution_order: choose the framework that best fits the inference type
map the secondary framework as cross-reference only
avoid double-counting the inference
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: one primary framework per inference dominates; the other is an annotation, never a parallel duplicate
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the two framings yield conflicting evaluations
conflict_axes.example: an expert-opinion inference framed both as a warrant and a scheme

conflict_axes.trigger: a fully faithful diagram can become unreadably dense
resolution_order: keep the diagram structurally complete
use a numbered statement key for detail
split very large maps by sub-argument
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: structural fidelity dominates readability; readability is recovered by keys and decomposition, not by dropping relations
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if simplification would delete a real support or attack relation
conflict_axes.example: a map so dense that arrows obscure the structure

conflict_axes.trigger: a portable notation may not express undercutters, qualifiers, or rebuttals
resolution_order: choose a notation expressive enough for the map
if none fits, keep the richer diagram authoritative
record relations lost in serialization
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: representational fidelity dominates portability; the expressive diagram is canonical when the notation cannot encode a relation
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if interchange requires dropping a relation the evaluation depends on
conflict_axes.example: exporting to a format that cannot encode inference-undercut

conflict_axes.trigger: a structurally perfect map can still rest on false or irrelevant premises
resolution_order: complete and validate the structure first
then assess acceptability, relevance, and sufficiency
keep the two judgments separate
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: structure must be settled before evaluation, but a coherent structure never substitutes for premise acceptability
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a coherent map is presented as if it established the conclusion
conflict_axes.example: a valid-looking diagram of an unsound argument

conflict_axes.trigger: a one-author support map can miss the dispute structure of an exchange
resolution_order: determine whether the text is a monologue or a dispute
use box-arrow mapping for monological support
use critical-discussion stages for disputes
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: the discourse type dictates the method; disputes require the dialectical reconstruction, not a one-sided support map
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a genuine exchange is mapped as a single author's argument
conflict_axes.example: mapping a debate as if only one side argued

edge_cases.trigger: a supplied premise makes the argument weaker than the arguer intended
edge_cases.example: inserting an obviously false universal to make the argument look fallacious
edge_cases.detection_method: check each supplied premise against the principle of charity and the arguer's commitments
resolution: replace with the minimally strong attributable premise

edge_cases.trigger: co-dependent premises drawn as independent supports
edge_cases.example: two premises that only work jointly shown with separate arrows
edge_cases.detection_method: apply the independence/suppression test to every multi-premise inference
resolution: redraw under a single inference node

edge_cases.trigger: the warrant is listed as just another datum
edge_cases.example: a general licensing principle placed in the data slot
edge_cases.detection_method: verify the warrant is a general inference license distinct from the case-specific data
resolution: move the licensing statement to the warrant slot

edge_cases.trigger: a hedged claim is mapped and evaluated as categorical
edge_cases.example: reading 'probably X' as 'X' in the conclusion
edge_cases.detection_method: compare the claim's modality in the map against the source wording
resolution: bound the verdict to the qualified claim

edge_cases.trigger: an inference is matched to the wrong scheme
edge_cases.example: a sign argument labeled as cause-to-effect
edge_cases.detection_method: check that every scheme slot binds and that the critical questions fit the inference
resolution: rebind slots and re-apply the correct critical questions

edge_cases.trigger: a move is called fallacious without establishing its discussion stage
edge_cases.example: labeling a clarification request as an evasion
edge_cases.detection_method: confirm the stage assignment before attributing a rule violation
resolution: re-evaluate the move against the stage-appropriate rule

edge_cases.trigger: a statement ends up supporting itself through a chain
edge_cases.example: premise A supports B which supports A
edge_cases.detection_method: run an acyclicity check over the support relations
resolution: break the cycle by re-examining roles

edge_cases.trigger: a statement neither supports anything nor is supported
edge_cases.failure_mode: dangling node left in the map
edge_cases.example: an extracted sentence that turns out non-argumentative
edge_cases.detection_method: check every node for at least one incoming or outgoing relation
resolution: remove the node or connect it

edge_cases.trigger: serialization drops a relation the notation cannot express
edge_cases.example: a tool without undercut support silently omits inference attacks
edge_cases.detection_method: round-trip the serialization and diff it against the source diagram

edge_cases.trigger: an explanation of an accepted fact is mapped as an argument
edge_cases.example: treating 'the ground is wet because it rained' as proving it rained
edge_cases.detection_method: test whether the conclusion is in dispute or already accepted

edge_cases.trigger: an intermediate conclusion is treated only as a premise
edge_cases.example: a lemma shown as a primitive premise with no support of its own
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether any premise is itself the target of support
resolution: mark the statement as an intermediate conclusion

edge_cases.trigger: a scheme is attributed that the arguer did not employ
edge_cases.example: casting a careful analogy as a hasty generalization
edge_cases.detection_method: check scheme attribution against the source's evident reasoning pattern
resolution: re-select a scheme consistent with the text

workflow.objective: extract the argument and assign inferential roles
acceptance_tests: each span is inferential
every statement has an inferential role
workflow.do_first_because: nothing downstream is valid unless the right material is extracted and its roles fixed

workflow.objective: standardize propositions and order the conclusion hierarchy
acceptance_tests: each proposition is declarative and faithful
the final conclusion is unique
workflow.do_first_because: clear, ordered propositions are the substrate every structural and Toulmin step needs

workflow.objective: supply unstated premises under charity and audit fidelity
acceptance_tests: each added premise is necessary and attributable
distortions are flagged
workflow.do_first_because: filling gaps before typing fixes the premise set so structure is typed only once

workflow.objective: type the support topology and model attacks
acceptance_tests: each inference is typed
attacks are typed and aimed correctly
workflow.do_first_because: the support topology determines both the diagram and the framework mappings

workflow.objective: map the inference onto Toulmin slots and an argumentation scheme
acceptance_tests: Toulmin slots populated and distinct
scheme slots bound and critical questions applied
workflow.do_first_because: framework analysis enriches each typed inference and supplies evaluation criteria

workflow.objective: reconstruct disputes as critical discussions when the text is dialogical
acceptance_tests: standpoints and difference of opinion stated
fallacies tied to violated rules
workflow.do_first_because: dialogical material needs the critical-discussion reconstruction a monological map cannot give

workflow.objective: render the map and serialize it in a chosen notation
acceptance_tests: the diagram reproduces the typed topology
serialization round-trips without loss
workflow.do_first_because: a faithful diagram must exist and be portable before validation and handoff

workflow.objective: validate the map for internal coherence and binding fidelity
acceptance_tests: no circular or dangling support
diagram matches typed structure
workflow.do_first_because: structural defects must be cleared before any evaluation or lock

workflow.objective: evaluate the argument by RSA criteria and lock the reconstruction
acceptance_tests: each premise judged acceptable and relevant
joint sufficiency assessed and high-risk nodes reviewed
workflow.do_first_because: locking requires coherence, charity audit, and human review of all high-risk reconstruction steps to pass

priority_rationale.notes: root intake all reconstruction inherits
role assignment is the backbone of every map
clear propositions precede all structural work
the chain must be ordered before typing and gap-filling
supplying premises fixes the premise set, high risk if uncharitable
governs faithfulness of the whole reconstruction
the topology drives the diagram and framework mappings
resolves the hardest structural ambiguity
captures defeasibility before evaluation
claim/data/warrant precedes backing and qualifier
explicit warrant precedes its backing and exceptions
qualifier bounds the eventual verdict
the scheme supplies the critical questions
turns a scheme match into an evaluation
confrontation fixes the dispute for dialectical reconstruction
stages contextualize rule checking
diagnoses fallacies as rule violations
the map must exist before serialization and validation
portable serialization of the map
coherence gate before evaluation and lock
final RSA verdict the map was built to support

dominance_rules.trigger: reconstruction would make the argument stronger than the arguer's commitment
dominance_rules.rule: fidelity to the arguer's actual commitment dominates making the argument maximally strong
dominance_rules.required_action: reconstruct the strongest reading the arguer would accept, not a better one
dominance_rules.example: reject a sophisticated premise a layperson plainly did not intend

dominance_rules.trigger: an argument is criticized on an uncharitable reading
dominance_rules.rule: the charitable reading dominates an easy-to-refute reading before any critique
dominance_rules.required_action: evaluate only after fixing the strongest attributable reconstruction
dominance_rules.example: do not refute a straw version when a stronger reading is available

dominance_rules.trigger: a tidy diagram conflicts with the correct support typing
dominance_rules.rule: correct structural typing dominates diagram tidiness
dominance_rules.required_action: redraw the diagram to match the typed structure
dominance_rules.example: split a dense map rather than mislabel linked support as convergent

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value mapping step is attempted before its prerequisite
dominance_rules.required_action: complete the prerequisite node before the dependent one
dominance_rules.example: do not type structure before the premise set is fixed by reconstruction

dominance_rules.trigger: numeric estimates are presented without eligible evidence
dominance_rules.required_action: label all estimates heuristic absent eligible data
dominance_rules.example: do not label a guessed relation strength as observed

dominance_rules.trigger: a reconstruction is about to be locked before validation passes
dominance_rules.rule: coherence and binding QA dominate locking
dominance_rules.required_action: block hard lock until the coherence report is clean
dominance_rules.example: no lock while a dangling node or circular support remains

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-risk reconstruction or evaluation decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automated acceptance for high-risk nodes
dominance_rules.required_action: route the decision to human review before lock
dominance_rules.example: supplied premises and fallacy attributions require human sign-off

dominance_rules.trigger: an inference is forced into a default or familiar scheme
dominance_rules.rule: best scheme fit dominates analyst familiarity
dominance_rules.required_action: select the scheme whose pattern and critical questions match the inference
dominance_rules.example: do not default every authority citation to a single scheme

dominance_rules.trigger: a verdict is stronger than the claim's qualifier permits
dominance_rules.rule: the claim's qualifier dominates verdict strength
dominance_rules.required_action: bound the evaluation to the qualified claim
dominance_rules.example: do not certify a categorical conclusion from a hedged claim

dominance_rules.trigger: a notation cannot encode a relation the evaluation needs
dominance_rules.required_action: keep the expressive diagram canonical and record serialization losses
dominance_rules.example: do not drop undercutters just because the export format lacks them

dominance_rules.trigger: a genuine dispute is mapped as one author's argument
dominance_rules.rule: for disputes, dialectical reconstruction dominates a one-sided support map
dominance_rules.required_action: reconstruct the critical-discussion stages for dialogical material
dominance_rules.example: map a debate as an exchange of standpoints, not a single argument

dominance_rules.trigger: a map element is added without traceability to a question or source
dominance_rules.required_action: link each element to a competency question and source
dominance_rules.example: drop a node that answers no analytic aim

anti_rework_rules.rule: extract and bound the argument before assigning roles
anti_rework_rules.rationale: typing non-argument text wastes effort and pollutes the map
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: roles assigned to spans later found non-argumentative
anti_rework_rules.example: classifying an explanatory sentence as a premise

anti_rework_rules.rule: assign inferential roles before standardizing propositions
anti_rework_rules.rationale: standardizing before roles can blur premise/conclusion distinctions
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a rewrite that changes a statement's apparent role
anti_rework_rules.example: paraphrasing a conclusion into a premise-like form

anti_rework_rules.rule: standardize propositions before supplying unstated premises
anti_rework_rules.rationale: adding premises to vague text creates noise that must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: supplied premises that target an unstandardized wording
anti_rework_rules.example: filling a gap in a rhetorical question before converting it

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete charitable reconstruction before typing the structure
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a premise added after typing can flip convergent to linked, forcing re-typing
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: structure re-typed after a late premise addition
anti_rework_rules.example: typing as convergent then adding a premise that makes it linked

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize support typing before drawing the diagram
anti_rework_rules.rationale: diagramming before typing yields a picture that must be redrawn
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a diagram revised after the typing is settled
anti_rework_rules.example: drawing separate arrows then re-joining them as linked

anti_rework_rules.rule: state the warrant explicitly before seeking its backing
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hunting for backing without a stated warrant is unfocused
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: backing collected for an unstated warrant
anti_rework_rules.example: listing supporting facts before naming the inference license

anti_rework_rules.rule: select the scheme before applying its critical questions
anti_rework_rules.rationale: applying the wrong question set misdirects scrutiny and is redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: critical questions applied that do not fit the inference
anti_rework_rules.example: asking causal questions of an argument from analogy

anti_rework_rules.rule: map discussion stages before checking rule violations
anti_rework_rules.rationale: labeling fallacies without stage context produces mislabels to redo
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a fallacy attributed before the move's stage is known
anti_rework_rules.example: calling a clarification request an evasion

anti_rework_rules.rule: draw the diagram before choosing a notation/tool
anti_rework_rules.rationale: committing to a notation before the diagram risks an ill-fitting schema
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a tool chosen that cannot express the drawn relations
anti_rework_rules.example: selecting a format that lacks undercut support

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate map coherence before evaluating the argument
anti_rework_rules.rationale: evaluating an incoherent map yields a verdict that must be discarded
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: an evaluation produced over an unvalidated map
anti_rework_rules.example: judging sufficiency on a map with a circular support loop

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the charity/fidelity audit before hard-locking
anti_rework_rules.rationale: locking a distorted reconstruction forces a full redo at review
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hard lock attempted with unflagged distortions
anti_rework_rules.example: locking a map built on an uncharitable added premise

anti_rework_rules.rule: complete the traceability matrix before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: untraceable map elements cause rework at review
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: hard lock attempted with incomplete traceability
anti_rework_rules.example: a node with no linked competency question surviving to lock

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and irreversibility
action: sort defects by risk and reversibility
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects scheduled first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only low-risk below tolerance

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-coupling node changes (extraction, roles, structure)
iteration_protocol.detection: trace edges from the changed node
action: flag affected typing and framework maps
acceptance_tests: all downstream dependents identified

iteration_protocol.detection: map defect type to repair owner via repair_routing
acceptance_tests: defect routed to a valid owner

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run the validator and formula checks
acceptance_tests: no new failures introduced

iteration_protocol.trigger: a premise is supplied or removed after typing
iteration_protocol.detection: detect a reconstruction change downstream of typing
acceptance_tests: typing consistent with the new premise set

iteration_protocol.trigger: critical questions for a scheme systematically fail
iteration_protocol.detection: check unanswered critical questions against the scheme
action: rebind slots and re-apply critical questions
acceptance_tests: the new scheme's pattern and questions fit
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: best-fitting scheme found or two re-selections done

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk reconstruction or fallacy attribution cannot be auto-repaired
acceptance_tests: high-risk defect has a review owner

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changes after a downstream lock
acceptance_tests: dependent locks downgraded

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new reconstruction version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version baseline
acceptance_tests: no validity regression versus baseline
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no regression or accepted with record
